subject: EU residency: temporary egress windows, key residency, and subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Elena Novak <dpo@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:15:00 +0100
Subject: Residency confirmation and temporary egress policy

Hi Ben,

Quick intro — I'm Elena, DPO at Acme Health. We're evaluating Redwood for inference across medical records and need to confirm a few residency points before legal can sign the DPA addendum. Our primary asks: 

- Can Redwood guarantee that patient-identifiable requests originating from EU customers are pinned to EU-hosted inference and storage?
- In the event of an outage, what is the maximum temporary egress/replication window you allow before failback? We need the number of hours and any alerting/approval processes.
- Do you support customer-controlled KMS keys with key material resident in the EU?
- Please provide a current subprocessor roster (or an escrowed list) and SOC2 + any relevant penetration test reports.

I've attached a short questionnaire (residency-questionnaire.xlsx) that legal/security would like you to fill.

Given the sensitivity, can we get these details in writing and an estimate for evidence delivery timelines?

Thanks,
Elena Novak
Data Protection Officer
Acme Health
Attachment: residency-questionnaire.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation and temporary egress policy

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Jonas (solutions) to get you definitive, evidence-backed answers. Summary from our side: 

- Region pinning: Redwood supports customer-level region pinning. When a customer requests EU pinning we will route inference and short-term storage to EU-hosted capacity and key materials can be kept in EU KMS where the customer opts for customer-managed keys.
- Temporary egress/failover: Our standard emergency failover is configurable; the default transient replication window is 72 hours for cross-region recovery, but that's negotiable in DPA addenda for enterprise customers. We can propose a shorter hard limit with additional operational controls (e.g., prior approval, advance notification, and automated audit logs).
- KMS: We support BYOK (customer-managed keys) with region-bound key stores (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS in eu-west-1 / etc.).
- Subprocessors & evidence: we can provide a current subprocessor roster and SOC2 Type II report via secure link or NDAd shared Drive.

Next steps: Jonas will propose a technical evidence pack and Marissa will propose DPA language for a lowered egress window if required. I'll book 30 mins for a quick tabletop if that helps. Attaching our public residency playbook for context.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-residency-playbook.pdf (PDF)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <dpo@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation and temporary egress policy

Hi Elena — 

Thanks for the questionnaire. I've started a draft DPA addendum that captures: EU-pin as default for your tenant, explicit commitment to limit temporary cross-border replication to a customer-negotiated maximum, and obligations around notification and auditability. For enterprise customers we typically add: 

- A maximum transient egress window in hours (we can commit to 24 / 48 / 72 as negotiated)
- Prior written approval for non-routine cross-border processing beyond the window
- Provision of SOC2 Type II and recent penetration test summaries within 5 business days of request (subject to NDAs)

Please review the attached draft (DPA_addendum_draft.docx) and mark any redlines. If Acme needs a binding 24-hour hard cap, we can draft a clause with exceptions for force majeure and an escalation playbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
Attachment: DPA_addendum_draft.docx (DOCX)

Thanks Marissa — a few clarifications from our side after discussing with infra/security: 

- Because Acme processes regulated patient data, we need any default transient egress window limited to 24 hours for EU-pinned tenants. Exceptions must be documented, rare, and require an approval workflow.
- We need confirmation that audit logs will show which customer key (KMS key id) was used for each data access and that those logs will be retained for at least 1 year.
- Where BYOK is used, we require that key material remains resident in the EU and that Redwood cannot export key material to another region.
- Please provide the subprocessor roster and indicate which subprocessors process telemetry vs. inference execution vs. logging.

Attached is a short internal requirements document that lists the minimum items our procurement and security teams want to see. Can you confirm turnaround for the roster and SOC2 link?

Regards,
Elena Novak
DPO, Acme Health
Attachment: org_requirements.pdf (PDF)

Hi Elena — Jonas here (Solutions). Quick technical answers and evidence plan: 

- 24-hour window: technically achievable. We will update the DPA addendum to include a 24-hour hard cap for transient cross-region replication for your tenant. That will be enforced by the routing layer and an automated rollback when capacity is restored.
- KMS / key residency: BYOK is supported. When you use a customer-managed key, the key identifiers and key material live in your chosen EU KMS (we never import/export your key material). We will provide a per-request audit record showing the key id used for each request; logs will be retained for 12 months by default (we can extend retention if needed).
- Subprocessor breakdown: we will provide a CSV that maps subprocessors to role: inference compute, telemetry/analytics, logging/storage. Expected delivery: 2 business days after NDA is completed.
- Evidence delivery: SOC2 Type II link (read-only secure link) + penetration test summary — target within 3 business days (post NDA).

Operational ask: can we run a short tabletop (30–45 mins) with Acme infra/security to walk through the pin + failover flow and approval steps? I pasted the HubSpot ticket for coordination: https://hubspot.example/contacts/HS-7842 and shared a Drive folder with the evidence set.

Happy to answer any technical follow-ups — we aim to have the DPA addendum with the 24-hour cap drafted by EOD Friday and the evidence links live early next week.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
